title: The Oath of the Weeping Wood
premise: Felix Fairweather, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Vess, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet spoken. When Felix finds tonight's date inscribed in the Weeping Wood, a prophecy-book carved into living trees a century ago, they learn the god's silence was not abandonment but imprisonment, and that Felix's own forgotten past is the key to freeing or destroying it. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitors and the rival Order of the Unblinking Eye, Felix must choose between erasing their memories forever and carrying forward a secret that could reignite the ancient war between gods and mortals. In the end, Felix breaks their oath deliberately, becoming the thirteenth witness whose testimony frees Vess—but at the cost of their own name, which they surrender willingly, finding belonging not in memory but in the family the guild has become.
about_author: Ansel Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and guild charters before turning to fiction. They write in a converted chapel on the Cornish coast, where they claim the ivy listens.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Felix Fairweather audits the Gilded Thorn's strangest accounts—a jar of last words, a debt paid in shadows—establishing their role as keeper of records and their quiet loneliness. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: competent detachment masking a hunger for belonging.

chapters.title: A God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: Felix performs the nightly oath-ritual to Vess and receives silence for the hundredth night, confiding in fellow guild member Odile that they fear their mercenary powers are fading. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: quiet dread of being abandoned mid-contract.

chapters.title: Tonight, Written a Century Ago
chapters.summary: Cataloguing a seized archive, Felix discovers the Weeping Wood—a book grown from tree-flesh—and finds tonight's date circled beside an image of a hooded figure holding a ledger. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: vertigo as invisibility collapses.

chapters.title: The Guild Takes Notice
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane reveals the Thorn has known about the Wood for years and forbids Felix from reading further; Odile warns that others who touched it vanished. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: betrayal—the family Felix trusted is hiding something.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor at the Door
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serah Vale arrives with a royal warrant for all prophecy-texts; Felix hides the Wood inside a ledger of debts and lies smoothly for the first time against their oath. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: exhilaration and guilt of deception.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Felix secretly returns to the archive; touching the Wood floods them with fragmented memories of a battlefield a century old—in which Felix themselves appears, unaged. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: horror of an impossible self.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile confesses she sold a memory of Felix to the Unblinking Eye years ago to pay her sister's ransom, explaining how the Order knows Felix's face. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: shame, and Felix's struggle between fury and forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: An astronomer-guild ally confirms the moon will complete a thirteenth turn in one month—an event that occurs only when a god's prison weakens. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dawning scale; this is bigger than one mercenary.

chapters.title: Vess Was Never Silent
chapters.summary: Felix deciphers marginalia showing Vess's 'silence' began when the god was sealed beneath the Weeping Wood itself after refusing to fight in the ancient war. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief reframed—the god didn't abandon them; the world abandoned the god.

chapters.title: Corvane's True Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix discovers Corvane's hidden accounts: the Thorn has been selling pieces of Vess's imprisoned power for decades, and Felix's contract was designed to keep them ignorant. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: cold rage; justice must come from outside every law they served.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Salt Marshes
chapters.summary: Exposed by the Eye, Felix flees with the Wood while Vale's soldiers burn the Thorn's outposts; Odile covers their escape and is captured. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Order of the Unblinking Eye
chapters.summary: Captured briefly by the Eye, Felix learns its Grandmaster was the mortal general who sealed Vess—and that his order has prolonged his life to guard the prison forever. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: unsettling sympathy for the enemy's conviction.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Escaping via a debt owed in shadows, Felix recovers Odile's sold memory and experiences their own century-old past: they were Vess's last sworn knight, made forgetful to survive the purge. POV: Felix (memory interludes). Emotional beat: identity shattering and reassembling.

chapters.title: Serah Vale's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vale corners Felix but hesitates—her warrant cites laws written by the same corrupt crown that funds the Thorn's trafficking. She lets Felix go, off the record. POV: Serah Vale. Emotional beat: an enemy choosing conscience over law.

chapters.title: The Chapel of Owed Debts
chapters.summary: Felix rallies scattered guild members who were cheated by Corvane, forging an unlikely company bound by shared grievance rather than oath. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: belonging found among the discarded.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Eye's Spire
chapters.summary: The company infiltrates the spire to free Odile; the heist succeeds but the Grandmaster unleashes a fragment of Vess's stolen power, leveling half the district. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Price of the Secret
chapters.summary: Felix realizes freeing Vess before the thirteenth turn completes would reignite the war; waiting means the god dies with the moon. There is no clean choice. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the weight of a secret no one should carry alone.

chapters.title: Confession Before the Company
chapters.summary: Felix tells the whole truth to their ragtag company—including their century-old identity—and asks them to decide together; Odile, freed and furious, votes to try anyway. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strength; trust as strategy.

chapters.title: The March on the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: The company fights through Vale's blockaded forest to reach the grove where the book grows from Vess's living body; Corvane arrives with hired legions to harvest the god entirely. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: desperate courage against impossible odds.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Oath
chapters.summary: At the grove's heart, Felix understands the seal requires a sworn knight's willing renunciation; they publicly break their oath—not in despair but as testimony, naming every crime committed in Vess's silence. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice transmuted into justice.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: As the moon completes its turn, Vess wakes—not to war but to witness; the god judges Corvane and the Grandmaster before mortal eyes, then chooses exile over vengeance, defusing the ancient conflict. POV: multiple, anchored to Felix. Emotional beat: awe, relief, and cost.

chapters.title: The Name Left Behind
chapters.summary: Felix surrenders their true name to complete the freeing, becoming simply 'the Keeper'; the rebuilt guild opens its ledgers to public audit, and Vale delivers a blank warrant—belonging, finally, freely given. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; memory lost, home found.
